description:
Find serialized uses of a C# script, the types it declares, or one of their members in scenes, prefabs, and assets. Check this alongside code references before renaming, moving, or deleting a type, serialized field, UnityEvent handler, or AnimationEvent method; zero code references alone is insufficient.

Without member, returns component attach points and ScriptableObject instances (by script GUID); [SerializeReference] instances of every type declared in the file and of their project subclasses/implementers, including instance types set by prefab instances, variants, and nested prefabs; and plain [Serializable] class/struct values reached through serialized fields (T, T[], List<T>, project generics, nested types, derived scripts) together with prefab overrides of those fields. Instances serialized under a [MovedFrom] legacy name, or stranded in a previous assembly (Unity loads those as missing types), are flagged. With member, searches that member's values in all of the above (including [FormerlySerializedAs] names and prefab-instance overrides), indexed UnityEvent method bindings (including broken/unbound targets), and project-wide AnimationEvents.

Requires the asset reference index; rescan from the UI if stale. GUID attach points match this exact script, so query other MonoBehaviour subclasses separately. Not covered: binary-serialized assets, Presets, custom serialization (ISerializationCallbackReceiver, dictionaries), and dynamic/string references.

file_path.description: Workspace-relative or absolute path to the .cs script file. Every class/struct/interface it declares is matched against [SerializeReference] data and plain [Serializable] field values.

member.description: Optional method or serialized-field name declared in that script (e.g. 'TakeDamage', 'maxHealth'). Omit to list the script's attach points, [SerializeReference] instances, and [Serializable] values instead.

max_results.description: Maximum usages to return. Default 100, max 400.
